text:
lucy_h: Heads up: starting v2 canary ramp at 11:30UTC. initial traffic 20% in us-east + eu-west.
deploy-bot: deploybot: canary rollout started by @maria_g — v2 -> 20% (regions: us-east, eu-west) — id: db-4419
maria_g: Pulling metrics and setting ops-eyes for the 11:30-12:30 window. cs notified.
chris_b: Quick check — did we include prefix cache warmup job in this deploy? last time warmup was skipped for a couple model variants.
lucy_h: Negative, warmup job was delayed due to packaging hiccup. I expect a short-lived spike while KV cache warms.
eng-runtime: Noted — runtime team watching KV eviction and mux timeouts. If we see >8% 5xx at p95 we recommend hitting the escape plan.
ops_jen: Seeing initial small blips: eu-west p95 latency up 1.8x but errors at 2% so far. continuing to monitor. :mag: 
lucy_h: ok let's let it run 10m then decide. if errors trend up we should reduce eu to 5% and pin high-traffic tenants.
deploy-bot: deploybot: automated probe scheduled: 11:42UTC health-checks every 30s for 10m
maria_g: If we need a quick mitigation, prefer tenant-level fallback to v1 rather than global rollback. less customer impact.
chris_b: Agree. list of sensitive tenants: T-A1, T-RedwoodMobile, T-EdgeGames. Lucy can you confirm traffic split?
lucy_h: T-RedwoodMobile is heavy in eu-west (~18% of canary load). T-A1 ~4%.
ops_jen: Alert: eu-west p95 errors climbing — now 7.5% and still trending. I recommend throttling eu-west to 5% and pin T-RedwoodMobile -> v1.
lucy_h: doing manual commands now: `/deploybot set-regional-percentage db-4419 eu-west 5`
deploy-bot: deploybot: regional traffic updated — db-4419 eu-west set to 5% by lucy_h
lucy_h: pinning command: `curl -XPOST https://ops.redwood/route/pin -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant":"T-RedwoodMobile","route":"/v2/generate","to":"v1","reason":"canary kv warmup spike"}'`
deploy-bot: deploybot: pin applied: T-RedwoodMobile -> v1 (operator: lucy_h)
eng-runtime: After pin, mux timeouts subsided for that tenant, p95 dropped back to baseline in ~70s. KV miss ratio still somewhat elevated but within expected warmup pattern.
maria_g: Good. please add a note to release notes and internal ops runbook: "v2 canary requires explicit warmup for quantized variants — include warmup job in packaging step". Link: https://redwood.internal/releases/2026-03-v2-canary-notes
chris_b: Also recommend adding an automatic pre-warm for top-5 tenants to avoid tenant-visible blips.
lucy_h: Will file an issue and assign to eng-runtime — short-term: keep canary paused and we will resume when warmup job confirmed.
ops_jen: Pause command: `/deploybot pause-rollout db-4419`
deploy-bot: deploybot: rollout db-4419 paused at 20% (operator: ops_jen)
maria_g: Decision: pause for 90m, run warmup in staging and replay top-tenant traffic, then resume at 10% for 30m observation window. If p95 errors <3% we advance. If not, rollback plan B: full v1 fallback for affected routes.
eng-runtime: We'll run tracing on mux request fanout and KV populate sequence. cc @samir_r for telemetry diffs.
chris_b: CS: please prepare messaging for T-RedwoodMobile explaining temporary pin to v1 and that we're working on targeted warmup to avoid repeat.
lucy_h: Noted. I updated the internal deploy checklist to include explicit warmup step and a preflight to confirm KV hit-rate.
maria_g: tagging this thread for post-deploy review. If runtime finds a code fix, open a postmortem and include timeline + tenant impact.
ops_jen: I'll keep operator eyes on the pinned tenants and have rollback playbook on standby.
lucy_h: thanks all — saving logs and metrics to the release folder: `s3://redwood-release-logs/db-4419/`
deploy-bot: deploybot: paused rollout reminder — run `/deploybot resume db-4419` to continue after warmup validated.
